question.problem: Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{3},{t}^{2}-2⟩$ at the point where $t=3,$  valid for all  real values of $u?$
question.worked_solution:
At the point where $t=3,$ the vector ${r}^{′}(3)$ is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at $P$ can be parametrized as
 

$$
R(u)=r(3)+u{r}^{′}(3),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

 

First, we find $r(3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(3) & =⟨{3}^{3},{3}^{2}-2⟩ \\  & =⟨27,7⟩\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨3{t}^{2},2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${r}^{′}(t)$ at $t=3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(3) & =⟨3(3)^{2},2(3)⟩ \\  & =⟨27,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point where $t=3$ is

$$
R(u)=⟨27,7⟩+u⟨27,6⟩,\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
